raw_text: DHAKA (AP) — Bangladesh's government imposed a sweeping internet blackout and deployed the military Tuesday as student-led protests against the civil service quota system spiraled into the worst political violence the country has seen in over a decade. Hospital officials reported at least 39 deaths since the unrest intensified over the weekend. The United Nations called for restraint from all sides and urged the government to restore communications. Student leaders, communicating through intermittent satellite links, vowed to continue protests until the quota system is abolished. Neighboring India placed its eastern border forces on high alert amid concerns of a potential refugee crisis.
